clue.text: Lively family seen in "an acreage of commemorative photography"

definitions.text: Lively family seen in "an acreage of commemorative photography"

parts.words: Lively family seen in "an acreage of commemorative photography"
parts.note: the novelist Penelope Lively's quoted phrase describes the bound book of snapshots in which a family is kept

explanation.surface: A quotation from Penelope Lively about acres of family photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of mounted photographs is where a family's commemorative pictures are collected.

clue.text: Grand Duchess finds articles on road on the continent

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a is the other indefinite article
St is the abbreviation for street, a road
Asia is a continent

explanation.surface: A Russian grand duchess turns up on a road somewhere on the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets a road on the continent; 'on' twice just joins pieces, which run in answer order.
explanation.definitionFit: The youngest daughter of Tsar Nicholas II was a grand duchess of that name.

clue.text: Controversial playwright flouted ban he flouted

indicators.note: flouted means the rules were broken, so the letters of the words are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A provocative dramatist defied a ban placed on him.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue repeats 'flouted'; only the second works, as the anagram signal on BAN HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Brendan, the Irish dramatist of The Quare Fellow, was notorious for drink and rebellion.

clue.text: Kipling destination a symbol of the universe, at the end of the day

parts.note: a mandala is a circular Hindu or Buddhist emblem of the cosmos

indicators.note: at the end of tells us to take only the final letter of the word day

explanation.surface: A traveller finds a cosmic symbol at the close of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's poem has the road to this Burmese city as its destination.

clue.text: What the addresses of the Smiths received

definitions.text: What the addresses of the Smiths received

parts.words: What the addresses of the Smiths received
parts.note: James and Horace Smith's parodies were titled Rejected Addresses, so their addresses got a refusal

explanation.surface: A family named Smith learns how their letters were received.
explanation.walkthrough: Rejected Addresses (1812) was a book of parodies by the brothers James and Horace Smith, imagined as speeches turned down for the reopening of a London theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal is what a turned-down entry receives.

clue.text: Sister of Kronos, unable to fly

definitions.meaning: the Titaness who was the sister and wife of Kronos, mother of Zeus
the South American ratite bird that cannot take to the air

explanation.definitionFit: One name serves both the Greek Titaness and a flightless bird of the pampas.

clue.text: Book hotel in Cornwall

definitions.meaning: the old coaching inn on Bodmin Moor that the novel made famous

explanation.definitionFit: The du Maurier novel takes its title from a real inn on Bodmin Moor.

clue.text: Grey areas of Sayers trial participant

definitions.text: Grey areas of Sayers trial participant

parts.words: Grey areas of Sayers trial participant
parts.note: grey areas of sky, joined to a person who testifies at a trial, give the title of a Dorothy L. Sayers novel

explanation.surface: Uncertainties surround someone taking part in a trial in Sayers.
explanation.walkthrough: Clouds of Witness is the Sayers novel in which Lord Peter's brother is tried for murder; 'trial participant' is a witness.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey masses in the sky form the first word of the Sayers title.

clue.text: Club review

definitions.meaning: the London gentlemen's club in Pall Mall
a literary weekly of the nineteenth century of that name

explanation.definitionFit: Both the Pall Mall club and a Victorian literary periodical bear the name of Athena's temple.

clue.text: Maxwell protagonist from Cypriot territory

indicators.note: from shows the letters are taken out of the run of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A Maxwell hero comes from Cypriot land.
explanation.walkthrough: Gavin Maxwell's Ring of Bright Water is about his pet of that kind, Mijbil.
explanation.definitionFit: The central animal of Maxwell's memoir is a river mammal.

clue.text: Unexpectedly land it for religious writer

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests the letters of the next words turn up in a surprising order

explanation.surface: A religious author comes down to earth when least expected.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew, the English deist, wrote Christianity as Old as the Creation.

clue.text: Greek poet goes to America to expose conspirator's despatcher

parts.note: Pindar was the Greek lyric poet of odes
US is short for the United States, America

explanation.surface: A Greek poet travels to America to unmask a plotter's killer.
explanation.walkthrough: In Julius Caesar, Cassius has his bondman of that name kill him; 'goes to' and 'to expose' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's bondman despatches the conspirator Cassius at Philippi.

clue.text: Weapon for a Beaufort, perhaps

definitions.meaning: Cardinal Henry Beaufort was bishop of the see of that name

explanation.definitionFit: A rifle maker's name is also that of the English see held by Cardinal Beaufort.

clue.text: John Barth's leave

definitions.meaning: John Barth's 1982 novel subtitled A Romance
a period of paid leave from academic work

explanation.definitionFit: Barth's novel shares its title with an academic's year of leave from teaching.

clue.text: Tale-teller with big mouth in Italy

definitions.text: Tale-teller with big mouth in Italy

parts.words: Tale-teller with big mouth in Italy
parts.note: Italian bocca means mouth and the suffix -accio makes it big and ugly, giving the name of the Decameron's author

explanation.surface: A gossip in Italy who cannot keep quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Decameron is a hundred tales; in Italian 'boccaccia' is a big or coarse mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florentine author of the Decameron is the great storyteller of medieval Italy.

clue.text: Job's usual pace? Jingle required

parts.note: Mr Jingle's servant in Dickens's Pickwick Papers is named Job, and his surname begins with the name of a horse's usual brisk gait

explanation.surface: A man named Job keeps a steady gait while a jingle is called for.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Pickwick Papers, Jingle's manservant is Job, whose surname suggests a jogging gait. The clue has no letter count.
explanation.definitionFit: A brisk jogging gait is the usual pace of a horse between walk and canter.

clue.text: Greek poet with added string to his lyre

definitions.text: Greek poet with added string to his lyre

parts.words: Greek poet with added string to his lyre
parts.note: the Milesian poet and musician famed for adding strings to the kithara

explanation.surface: A Greek poet with another string to his bow.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes the idiom 'another string to his bow'; the poet of Miletus was said to have extended the lyre.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet of Miletus was censured in Sparta for adding strings to the kithara.

clue.text: He wrote a history of war in retrospect

definitions.text: He wrote a history of war in retrospect

parts.words: He wrote a history of war in retrospect
parts.note: In Retrospect is the title of the US Defense Secretary's 1995 book on Vietnam

explanation.surface: A military historian looks back on a war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retrospect' looks like a phrase of manner but is the book's title, In Retrospect: The Tragedy and Lessons of Vietnam.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert, Kennedy's Defense Secretary, wrote a memoir of the Vietnam War.

clue.text: Roguish start of a reviewed church history

indicators.note: start of tells us to take the opening letter of each of the four following words

explanation.surface: A mischievous opening to a reviewed history of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A roguish look is a knowing, mischievous one.

clue.text: Heresy of a different view of Occam's lion

indicators.note: of a different view says the letters of the next words are seen in another arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, its s counted as a letter

explanation.surface: A heresy holds an unusual opinion of Occam's lion.
explanation.definitionFit: Image-breaking was condemned as heresy in the Byzantine controversy.

clue.text: He was taken for a ride on his wedding anniversary

definitions.text: He was taken for a ride on his wedding anniversary

parts.words: He was taken for a ride on his wedding anniversary
parts.note: Cowper's linen-draper whose borrowed horse bolted with him on his wedding-day outing

explanation.surface: A man was cheated on his wedding anniversary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken for a ride' means cheated, but here it is literal: in Cowper's ballad John Gilpin's horse bolts past Edmonton.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowper's comic ballad tells of a London draper's runaway ride on his anniversary.

clue.text: An associate of publicans, according to Benson?

definitions.text: An associate of publicans, according to Benson?

parts.words: An associate of publicans, according to Benson?
parts.note: Benson's title pairs this strict Jewish sect member with the publicans, tax collectors of the Gospel parable

explanation.surface: A drinking companion of innkeepers, so Benson says.
explanation.walkthrough: Publicans here are the tax collectors of the Gospels, not innkeepers; Luke's parable sets one beside a member of the strict sect.
explanation.definitionFit: In Luke's parable a member of the strict Jewish sect prays beside a tax collector.

clue.text: Belloc's Trojan prince?

definitions.meaning: Hilaire Belloc's 1900 book about the French capital
Priam's son who carried off Helen

explanation.definitionFit: The French capital, subject of a Belloc book, shares its name with Helen's Trojan abductor.

clue.text: Village prince

definitions.meaning: a small settlement without a church

explanation.definitionFit: A small settlement shares its name with Shakespeare's Danish prince.

clue.text: A lover of Raphael

parts.note: the Italian painter Raphael, a man of the Romance peoples who loved, was a lover of the kind a stock phrase names after his race

explanation.surface: Someone who fell for the painter Raphael.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks for one of Raphael's mistresses, but Raphael himself, an Italian lover, was a stock 'Latin lover'.
explanation.definitionFit: Italians are a Romance-speaking people, and the stock phrase for a romantic Italian man begins with this word.

clue.text: That of Edmonton was 21's objective

parts.note: in Cowper's ballad the rider's party were to dine at an inn at Edmonton of that name

explanation.surface: Something in Edmonton was a rider's goal.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Diverting History of John Gilpin his wife waits for him at the Bell inn at Edmonton, which his horse carries him past.
explanation.definitionFit: The inn sign at Edmonton named the place where Gilpin's family planned to dine.

clue.text: Summary sort of caper seen on dust jacket

indicators.note: sort of hints at a rearranged version of the word caper

explanation.surface: A blurb summary of an escapade appears on a book's dust jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen on dust jacket' is a link describing where a book's summary is printed.
explanation.definitionFit: A short restatement of the main points is a summary.

clue.text: Kafka's piece may be taken on board

definitions.meaning: Kafka's unfinished novel about the land surveyor K.

definitions.text: piece may be taken on board
definitions.meaning: a chessman, the rook, which can be captured on the chessboard

explanation.definitionFit: Kafka's novel shares its title with the chess rook's other name.

clue.text: Bad lot for whom Hellman had time

definitions.text: Bad lot for whom Hellman had time

parts.words: Bad lot for whom Hellman had time
parts.note: Lillian Hellman's memoir of the McCarthy years is titled after a time of such rogues

explanation.surface: Hellman had time for a rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had time for' suggests liking someone; Hellman's book is Scoundrel Time.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad lot is a villain or rogue.

clue.text: Jamesian version of Sorel

parts.note: G. P. R. James wrote a historical novel about the mistress of Charles VII, whose first name is wanted

explanation.surface: A Henry James take on Sorel.
explanation.walkthrough: Agnes Sorel was mistress of Charles VII of France; G. P. R. James's novel bears her name.
explanation.definitionFit: The French royal mistress Sorel was known by this first name.
